speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with yellowish discoloration of the skin. To determine the cause, are you noticing this jaundice is appearing within the first 24 hours of birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding jaundice (suboptimal intake) or potentially physiological jaundice, given the onset at 5 days, full-term status, exclusive breastfeeding history, and lack of reported stool/urine changes. I recommend checking bilirubin levels to confirm the severity and rule out hemolysis. REQUEST TEST: Total_Bilirubin_Level. REQUEST TEST: Direct_Bilirubin_Level.
